title: Explicitly compute and decompose derived metrics defined in the rubric
when_to_use: When the task or rubric requires analysis of derived metrics (e.g., unit cost, weighted average) defined by specific formulas.
experience:
* Before any analysis, parse the rubric or task instruction for explicit metric definitions (e.g., 'unit freight = Σ(Shipping Cost) ÷ Σ(Quantity)').
* Compute each required derived metric separately and verify its components are correctly aggregated.
* If a proxy or alternative metric is used, justify why the required metric could not be computed and document the substitution.
* Always decompose derived metrics to understand their drivers (e.g., changes in unit freight can be due to changes in shipping cost mix vs. quantity mix).
* Compare the computed derived metric against simpler proxies (e.g., average shipping cost) to validate sensitivity.
checklist: List required derived metrics from the rubric/task
Compute each derived metric with the exact formula
If data is unreliable, note it and use proxy with justification
Document how the derived metric differs from a simple proxy
Include derived metric in all diagnostic steps it is required for
common_failure_prevented: This prevents missing the precise metric required for scoring, as happened with unit freight and weighted unit price, leading to rubric failures.

title: Perform comprehensive diagnostic analysis across all entities before zooming in
when_to_use: When the task requires investigating a fluctuation or change across a category (e.g., product category, region).
experience:
* After identifying a target entity (e.g., a product category with the largest swing), compute diagnostic metrics for all sub-entities (e.g., all products, all SKUs, all shipping methods) within that category.
* Aggregate or rank sub-entities by their contribution to the overall fluctuation (e.g., which products contribute most to margin change).
* Before drilling down into a single entity (e.g., one product), verify it is the primary driver by comparing its impact to the sum of all others.
* Use segmentation (e.g., terciles, quartiles) to group sub-entities by performance (e.g., high-margin vs. low-margin) and analyze shifts between segments.
* If focusing on a single entity, explicitly state that it was selected as the top contributor and summarize the diagnostic for all others.
checklist: Identify all relevant sub-entities within the target category
Compute diagnostic metric for each sub-entity
Rank or segment sub-entities by contribution to change
Confirm selected focus entity is the primary driver
If not, analyze the top contributors collectively
common_failure_prevented: This prevents narrow analysis of a single sub-entity (e.g., only Beds) when the rubric requires a comprehensive product-level or SKU-level diagnosis for the entire category.

title: Align segmentation and join logic with the task's temporal scope
when_to_use: When the task requires analyzing customer behavior (e.g., RFM) or engagement metrics over a specific time period (e.g., 2022–2024).
experience:
* Define the analysis time window explicitly (e.g., 'from 2022 through 2024').
* When creating segments (e.g., RFM), ensure all underlying data (orders, browsing) is filtered to the relevant time window unless otherwise stated.
* For engagement metrics tied to orders, join customer or product data only for the relevant time window and customer set (e.g., customers who bought the category in the period).
* If comparing core vs. non-core customers, define core using behavior within the same time window.
* When reporting trends per year, ensure yearly customer sets are defined separately (e.g., customers active each year) before aggregating metrics.
checklist: Explicitly note the required time window for analysis
Filter all source tables to the time window before joins/aggregates
When comparing groups (core/non-core), define them using window-specific data
For yearly trends, create separate yearly subsets before computing metrics
Document any deviations from window-based filtering
common_failure_prevented: This prevents analyzing engagement or customer segments with incorrectly aligned temporal logic, leading to misinterpretation of trends, as happened with browsing metrics not joined to yearly customer sets.
